note: THIS FILE IS THE MACHINE-GENERATED OUTPUT of weight_sync_bench.phase2.bf16_floor_v2's --sweep-seq-len mode, run on the box and pulled into the repo -- not hand-assembled from reported console output. It replaces an earlier hand-written version of this same file that was lost before it was committed; every number in 'configuration', 'environment' (other than the driver_version backfill noted there), 'sweep', 'results', and 'generated_at' is this run's own real output and has not been altered. This 'note' array re-adds the interpretation layer the lost hand-written version carried, checked against these actual numbers rather than the estimates that version used.

THE MEAN IS MEASURED INVARIANT ACROSS SEQ_LEN 8 TO 512 (A 64x RANGE), RETIRING THE PRACTICAL SEQ_LEN-DEPENDENCE CAVEAT FOR THE MEAN. mean_ulp across the sweep: 4.99 / 4.77 / 4.85 / 4.20 ULP at seq_len 8 / 32 / 128 / 512 (mean_deviation 3.895e-02 / 3.725e-02 / 3.791e-02 / 3.280e-02) -- a ~16% peak-to-trough spread with no monotonic trend, consistent with repetition-count sampling noise rather than a seq_len effect, and every point gates PASS. This is exactly the design's predicted behavior (see SPEC.md's mean-as-primary-statistic reasoning): the mean characterizes the per-element error distribution, and more prompt positions means more independent draws from that same distribution, not a different one.

THE MAX IS NOT EXPLAINED BY THE UNCONVERGED-ORDER-STATISTIC MECHANISM, AND AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS NOTE WAS WRONG TO SAY SO. max_ulp across the sweep: 104.0 / 168.0 / 1192.0 / 156.0 ULP (max_deviation 0.8125 / 1.3125 / 9.3125 / 1.21875) at seq_len 8 / 32 / 128 / 512. Phase 1's order-statistic finding (tolerance/phase1a.json) was a monotonic DRIFT UPWARD with more draws (11.5 -> 14 ULP going from 5 to 20 repetitions, same distribution, more samples from it). This sweep's pattern is not that: it spikes 7x at seq_len=128 and then falls back BELOW the seq_len=32 value at seq_len=512, despite seq_len=512 drawing from roughly 6.21 billion pooled elements (20 reps * 4 batch * 511 rows * 151936 vocab) against seq_len=128's ~1.54 billion (20 * 4 * 127 * 151936) -- about 4x more draws landing on a SMALLER max. An earlier version of this note called the seq_len=128 spike 'a clean, real illustration' of the order-statistic mechanism; that explains past the actual shape of the data (non-monotonic) rather than accounting for it, and is corrected here: THE SPIKE IS UNEXPLAINED, not attributed to a mechanism.

MAX DISCRIMINATING TEST: THREE DRAWS NOW, NOT TWO -- NOTHING FURTHER TO EXPLAIN. Three independently-seeded draws at the identical configuration (--repetitions 20 --batch 4 --seq-len 128): seed_base=0 gave max_ulp 1192.00 (max_deviation 9.3125, the original sweep point), seed_base=1000 gave 393.50 (3.074), seed_base=2000 gave 445.00 (3.4765625). Two of the three cluster near ~400 ULP and one sits about 2.8x higher (1192 / ((393.50+445.00)/2) = 2.84) -- a heavy-tailed distribution's shape with only three samples, not a new pattern needing its own account. None of the three values is stable across draws, none reproduces another, and none is closer to 'the' answer than the others -- CONCLUSION UNCHANGED FROM THE FIRST DISCRIMINATING TEST, NOW ON FIRMER FOOTING: the bf16 floor's max at this configuration is a tail statistic with genuine, large draw-to-draw variance. There is no single stable element to locate (a real single-element bug would reproduce; none of these three did), and no mechanism to attribute any individual value to beyond 'draw from a heavy tail.' The gate is unaffected -- it derives the threshold from the mean, not the max, and the mean's own three-draw stability is recorded separately below.

THE STRONGER ARGUMENT FOR MEAN-AS-PRIMARY IS THIS SPIKE'S MAGNITUDE, NOT A DRIFT STORY. At seq_len=128, max_deviation (9.3125) is ~245.6x the floor mean at that same point (3.791e-02) and ~3.63x the WEAKEST break case measured in that same run (case2_oproj_col_permute, mean_deviation 2.5637 -- the same-run, apples-to-apples comparison; against the canonical reproduction run's weakest break of 1.570, measured at a different seq_len, the ratio is ~5.93x, close to but not the same figure since it mixes runs). Either comparison lands in the same place: had the gate used max instead of mean as its statistic, this single point's noise floor would have exceeded a real injected layout bug -- the gate would have failed to distinguish 'correct execution, one outlier element' from 'genuinely broken sharding' at seq_len=128. That is a direct demonstration of why mean is the right primary statistic (SPEC.md's 'Change the primary statistic'), sharper than the general 'max is noisier than mean' framing this note previously led with.

DISCRIMINATING TEST FULL RESULTS, ALL DRAWS RECORDED. `--seed-base` (weight_sync_bench/phase2/collective_logits.py's `_run_worker`) shifts BOTH seed axes, not just tokens: token seed becomes `10_000 + seed_base + rep` (bf16_floor.py's `_seeded_token_batches`, called once for every repetition's tokens up front) and model seed becomes `seed_base + rep`, applied via `torch.manual_seed(...)` once per repetition inside the loop that follows -- this sets the global torch RNG, consulted by nothing in this configuration (greedy decoding, weights from disk, no dropout or speculative decoding), present so the hook is already threaded for a future non-greedy variant and so the harness matches phase 1's model_seeds convention. `--seed-base 0` (the default, omitted from every command below) reproduces the corresponding original sweep/reproduction point exactly, so each rerun below changes exactly one thing relative to its own seed_base=0 baseline: the prompt set (and model-seed sequence). Command form: `.venv-phase2/bin/python -m weight_sync_bench.phase2.bf16_floor_v2 --repetitions <N> --batch <B> --seq-len <S> --seed-base <K>`. Results: batch=4/seq_len=128/20 reps: seed_base=1000 -> mean_deviation 3.712e-02 (4.75 ULP), max_deviation 3.074 (393.50 ULP), case1_qkv_head_permute=3.201, case2_oproj_col_permute=2.596, case3_norm_permute=2.820, verdict PASS; seed_base=2000 -> mean_deviation 3.726e-02 (4.77 ULP), max_deviation 3.4765625 (445.00 ULP), case1=3.133, case2=2.602, case3=2.931, verdict PASS. batch=2/seq_len=8/20 reps (bf16_floor.py's run20_folded_in configuration): seed_base=1000 -> mean_deviation 3.865e-02 (4.95 ULP), max_deviation 0.9375 (120.00 ULP), case1_qkv_head_permute=1.862, case2_oproj_col_permute=1.648, case3_norm_permute=2.964, verdict PASS. See the notes above and below for what these establish about the max (heavy-tailed, no mechanism), the mean (invariant), and break-case/separation-ratio stability (config-dependent bands, not draw-dependent).

THE MEAN'S INVARIANCE IS NOW CONFIRMED ACROSS A FULL PROMPT-SET CHANGE, NOT JUST ACROSS SEQ_LEN -- STRONGER EVIDENCE THAN THE SWEEP ALONE. The discriminating rerun (--seed-base 1000, same seq_len=128) moved the mean only ~2.1% (3.791e-02 -> 3.712e-02, i.e. (3.791-3.712)/3.791 = 2.08%), landing inside the original sweep's own 3.280e-02 (seq_len=512) to 3.895e-02 (seq_len=8) band, despite drawing an entirely different set of 20*4=80 prompts and a different model-seed sequence. The seq_len sweep (see the mean-invariance note above) varies the SAMPLE COUNT at a fixed underlying error distribution -- more positions per prompt, same tokens-generation logic; this rerun instead varies the INPUT itself, entirely different tokens, at a FIXED seq_len. The mean held steady under both kinds of change, not just the sample-count one, which is the stronger of the two tests: it is easier to imagine sample-count invariance being an artifact of how the floor is computed than input invariance being one.

PROMPT-DRAW DEPENDENCE OF BREAK MAGNITUDES IS RETIRED, AT BOTH CONFIGURATIONS NOW MEASURED. An earlier version of this note reported break magnitudes moving at the 'tens-of-percent level' -- that finding was wrong, and was entirely an artifact of a three-way confound (comparing the smoke run [--batch 1 --seq-len 8 --repetitions 1], the reproduction [--batch 2 --seq-len 8 --repetitions 20], and the seed_base=1000 rerun [--batch 4 --seq-len 128 --repetitions 20] as if they differed only in prompt draw, when batch, seq_len, and repetition count all differed too). With batch, seq_len, and repetitions actually held fixed and only the prompt draw varied, at TWO independent configurations, break magnitudes are stable: batch=4/seq_len=128/20 reps (seed_base 0/1000/2000) -- mean 3.791e-02/3.712e-02/3.726e-02 (2.1% spread), case2 (weakest throughout) 2.564/2.596/2.602 (1.5% spread), case1 3.160/3.201/3.133, case3 3.001/2.820/2.931; batch=2/seq_len=8/20 reps (seed_base 0/1000) -- mean 3.898e-02/3.865e-02 (0.8% apart), case2 (weakest throughout) 1.570/1.648 (5.0% apart), case1 1.772/1.862, case3 2.984/2.964. Every spread is single-digit-percent. There is no residual prompt-draw-dependence question left open at either configuration.

THE SEPARATION RATIO IS A FUNCTION OF CONFIGURATION, NOT OF DRAW -- RECORD BOTH BANDS. At batch=2/seq_len=8/20 reps: 40.3x (seed_base=0) and 42.6x (seed_base=1000), 5.7% apart -- tight within itself across two independent prompt sets. At batch=4/seq_len=128/20 reps: 67.6x / 69.9x / 69.8x (seed_base 0/1000/2000), under 2.1% apart across three independent prompt sets -- also tight within itself. The ~1.7x gap BETWEEN the two bands (67-70x vs 40-43x) is a real configuration effect (batch and/or seq_len change the floor-mean-to-break-magnitude relationship), not draw noise -- each band's own internal spread is far smaller than the gap between bands. batch=2/seq_len=8 is the BINDING (narrower) configuration and the one this project's break cases run at by default.

SAFETY_FACTOR=15 x GATE_MARGIN=2 = 30 IS NOW VALIDATED AGAINST THE BINDING CONFIGURATION'S MEASURED BAND, NOT A SINGLE DRAW. The binding band (batch=2, seq_len=8, 20 reps) is 40.3x-42.6x across two independent prompt draws (see the band note above). 30 stays strictly under both observed points, with ~34% headroom at the narrowest ((40.3-30)/30): the budget would need to be enlarged by more than a third before a draw at this measured band could threaten it. This is measurement of a band, not proof of a lower bound -- a third or later draw at batch=2/seq_len=8 could in principle land narrower than 40.3x, the same caveat the max-discriminating-test note applies to itself -- but two independent draws landing within 5.7% of each other is meaningfully stronger support than the single 40.3x observation this constant was originally set against. weight_sync_bench/phase2/bf16_floor.py's SAFETY_FACTOR comment has been updated to cite this measured band instead of the single prior observation. Constants are UNCHANGED by this note -- it records that the existing 15/2 split has more support than when it was chosen, not a case for retuning it.

THE SAME-RUN EVIDENCE FOR MEAN-AS-PRIMARY IS STRONGER STILL: THE MEAN AT SEQ_LEN=128 IS UNMOVED BY THE SAME OUTLIER THAT SHIFTED THE MAX 7x. The four sweep means are 3.895e-02 / 3.725e-02 / 3.791e-02 / 3.280e-02 at seq_len 8/32/128/512 -- seq_len=128's mean (3.791e-02) sits well inside that overall range, close to its immediate neighbour at seq_len=32 (3.725e-02, ~1.8% apart) and higher than seq_len=512's (3.280e-02), with nothing in its position marking it as the point that also happens to contain a 1192-ULP outlier. The arithmetic explains why: the outlier element (9.3125) is one value among 4 (batch) * 127 (rows) * 151936 (vocab) = 77,183,488 elements in the single repetition-cell that contains it, so it contributes 9.3125 / 77,183,488 =~ 1.2065e-07 to that cell's own mean -- about 5.5 orders of magnitude (a factor of ~3.18e-06) below the reported mean_deviation (3.791e-02), not the 'roughly four orders' a rougher estimate might suggest. One anomalous element can move a max by 7x while being arithmetically invisible to a mean averaged over tens of millions of siblings; that is the concrete, same-run, measured case for mean-as-primary, stronger than any comparison across runs or against break-case values.

REPRODUCTION AT --repetitions 20 --batch 2 --seq-len 8 (bf16_floor.py's run20_folded_in configuration, reported separately from the sweep this file records -- not itself part of this JSON's 'sweep'/'results' data, which is batch=4 throughout) matched tolerance/phase2a_bf16_floor.json to four significant figures: mean_deviation 3.898e-02, max_deviation 8.125e-01 (104.00 ULP), and break-case means 1.772 / 1.570 / 2.984, against enable_prefix_caching=False here versus True in the original measurement. This resolves tolerance/phase2a_bf16_floor.json's recorded caveat that repetition independence under prefix caching was unverified: had caching been silently correlating repetitions, turning it off would have moved the mean by more than four-significant-figure noise; it did not. See tolerance/phase2a_bf16_floor.json's own updated note for the full comparison.

SMOKE RUN, FULLY ATTRIBUTED -- CONFIGURATION: --repetitions 1 --batch 1 --seq-len 8 (this was the first end-to-end execution of bf16_floor_v2.py; also reported separately, not part of this file's sweep data, which is batch=4 throughout). Full result: mean_deviation 3.038e-02, max_deviation 2.500e-01, threshold 4.557e-01, break-case means case1_qkv_head_permute=1.604, case2_oproj_col_permute=1.644, case3_norm_permute=2.464, gating PASS. The mean is about 22% below the --repetitions 20 --batch 2 --seq-len 8 reproduction value (3.898e-02); batch (1 vs 2) and repetitions (1 vs 20) both differ too, so this is not a pure repetitions-only comparison -- recorded as observed, as a datapoint on how much a quick smoke run's floor number should be trusted before a full run confirms it. THESE THREE BREAK-CASE VALUES (1.604/1.644/2.464) WERE PREVIOUSLY RECORDED ELSEWHERE IN THIS ARTIFACT WITHOUT THIS CONFIGURATION LABEL, INCORRECTLY COMPARED AGAINST THE seed_base=1000, batch=4, seq_len=128 DRAW AS IF THAT WERE A CLEAN PROMPT-DEPENDENCE TEST -- corrected below; that comparison mixed three different configurations (batch, seq_len, and repetition count all differed alongside the prompt draw) and was not evidence about prompt-draw dependence at all.

THE SEQ_LEN=512 RUN MOVED ROUGHLY 1.2GB PER CALL THROUGH THE BYTE-BUFFER TRANSPORT (collective_logits.py Q7) WITHOUT FAILURE, pushing the file-handoff-reconsideration threshold that module's docstring names well past its previously-exercised ~77MB figure (tolerance/phase2b_extraction.json, seq_len=128) into multi-GB territory. A single reconstructed tensor at seq_len=512 is [511, 151936] float32 =~ 310MB; under TP=2's all-gather branch (confirmed active on this box, collective_logits.py Q3 revised), the collective_rpc call carries one such tensor back from each rank, roughly 620MB combined -- the reported ~1.2GB is about 2x that, not exactly reconciled (possible encode/decode/framing overhead not captured by the raw tensor arithmetic), recorded as reported rather than forced to match.

supersedes: Supersedes tolerance/phase2a_bf16_floor.json on extraction path and cache flags only, while measuring the same quantity (TP1-vs-TP2 mean absolute logit deviation under bf16, and the same three break-case injections against it). Extraction: collective_rpc (weight_sync_bench.phase2.collective_logits.run_one_prompt) instead of SamplingParams(prompt_logprobs=-1) plus a Python-object scatter loop -- see tolerance/phase2b_extraction.json for the bit-identity and timing verification this port relies on. Cache flags: enable_chunked_prefill=False and enable_prefix_caching=False are now set explicitly (bf16_floor.py leaves both at vLLM's defaults, i.e. on); this resolves tolerance/phase2a_bf16_floor.json's own recorded caveat that repetition independence under prefix caching was unverified there -- in this artifact independence is guaranteed by construction, not merely assumed, and a separate same-configuration reproduction run confirmed the numbers match to four significant figures (see this file's 'note' array). SAFETY_FACTOR, GATE_MARGIN, the mean-as-primary-statistic rule, the differential TP1-vs-TP2 design, and every break-case injection are unchanged -- imported directly from bf16_floor.py, not re-derived. THIS FILE IS THE OUTPUT of that measurement composition (the full repetitions/TP2/break-case/gate pipeline) run end to end with the new extraction path on real hardware -- the 'sweep'/'results' data below is that execution's own output, not a projection from the underlying run_one_prompt primitive's verification (tolerance/phase2b_extraction.json), which was a separate, earlier, single-prompt check.

environment.driver_version_note: Recorded as null by this run because weight_sync_bench.phase2.bf16_floor.environment() guarded torch.cuda.driver_version with hasattr(), and that attribute does not exist on torch 2.13.0+cu130 -- the guard silently fell through to None on every real run including this one, instead of raising on a wrong assumption. This is the same failure class as collective_logits.py's earlier `shape[0] >= expected_min_positions` bug (fixed to an exact `==`): a loose guard around instrumentation that degrades silently rather than surfacing that its assumption no longer holds. Concretely, every phase-2 artifact through this one recorded driver_version as null while the box was reporting 580.126.16 the entire time (matches tolerance/phase2a_bf16_floor.json's run20_folded_in and tolerance/phase2b_extraction.json exactly), and nothing in the pipeline ever surfaced that mismatch -- it took a human reading this artifact next to the box's own output to notice. Filled in here now that it's known, and environment() has been fixed (nvidia-smi subprocess, same pattern as the existing git_commit capture -- there was never a torch attribute to guard correctly in the first place) so future runs record it directly instead of needing this kind of backfill.
